title: Material Instances 🧬
description: Create flexible materials with exposed parameters without recompiling.

slides.title: Master vs Instance 👑
slides.content:
# One Material, Many Looks

A **Material Instance** is a child of a parent (Master) material. It lets you change parameters without recompiling the shader – which is **fast** and **efficient**.

* **Master Material** – contains the full node graph. Parameters are exposed.
* **Material Instance** – overrides those parameters with different values (colours, textures, scalars).

*Analogy:* The Master is a **cake recipe**. Instances are individual cakes with different toppings and fillings, but the same base.

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of Material Instances?

options.text: They are easier to create than master materials
Changing parameters does not require shader recompilation
They can have completely different node graphs
They render faster than master materials

quizData.explanation: Material Instances reuse the compiled shader from the parent, so parameter changes are instant and cheap.

slides.title: Creating Parameters in the Master 🛠️
slides.content:
## Make It Flexible

Instead of a hard‑coded Constant node, use a **Scalar Parameter** (keyboard: hold **S** + click) or **Vector Parameter** (hold **V** + click).

* **Scalar Parameter** – a named float (e.g., `RoughnessAmount`)
* **Vector Parameter** – a named colour (e.g., `TintColor`)
* **Texture Sample Parameter** – a named texture slot (right‑click → Texture → Texture Sample Parameter2D)

When you create a Material Instance from this master, these parameters appear in the Details Panel, ready to be changed.

slides.title: Making an Instance 👶
slides.content:
## Step by Step

1. Create a **Master Material** with parameters (e.g., `M_Master`).
2. Right‑click the master → **Create Material Instance**.
3. Name it (e.g., `MI_RedPlastic`).
4. Double‑click the instance. You'll see a list of overridable parameters.
5. Check the box next to a parameter to override, then set a new value.
6. Apply and save.

Now you can create dozens of instances from one master: `MI_BlueMetal`, `MI_RoughConcrete`, etc., all at near‑zero performance cost.

quizData.question: To create a colour parameter in a Master Material, hold the _____ key and click in the graph.
quizData.explanation: Hold V + click for Vector Parameter (colour). Hold S + click for Scalar Parameter.

slides.title: Static Switch Parameters 🔀
slides.content:
## Compile‑Time Branches

A **Static Switch Parameter** (keyboard: hold **S** + click, then select from list) allows you to switch between two material paths at instance level, but **this recompiles** a new shader variant.

Use it for:
* Toggling a feature on/off (e.g., use Normal Map? yes/no)
* Switching between two texture sets

Be conservative; each switch combination creates a new shader permutation, increasing compile time and memory.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Parameter Groups

In the Master Material, select a parameter node → Details → **Group** → type a category name (e.g., "Colour"). In the instance, parameters appear neatly grouped, saving you scrolling time.
